full_judgment:
Mohammad Gholam Rabbani J : This Rule under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is against the petitioners' conviction and sentence vide judgment and order dated 3-2-94 passed by the Additional Anti-Terrorism Tribunal No. 3, Dhaka in Anti-Terrorism Case No. 255 of 1998. Petitioners were tried in absentia and were convicted under section 4 of the Anti-Terrorism Act of 1992 and each was sentenced to suffer RI for 5 years and also to pay fine. 

 2. It is not necessary to state the prosecution case or to consider the evidence on record as, it appears, the Rule was issued only on the ground as stated in the Rule application to the effect that the impugned conviction awarded to the petitioners in absentia was illegal and liable to be set aside as there were no materials on record to show that they absconded or they avoided arrest or there was no immediate prospect of their arrest. It is stated in the Rule application that the petitioners learnt about their conviction and sentence on a later date on 11-6-97 from the local police station and then surrendered on 12-6-97. 

 3. Mr. Khandker Mahbub Hossain, learned Advocate for the petitioners, at first reads sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Anti-Terrorism Act and then reads order No.2 dated 25-7-93 and order No.8 dated 7-8-93 of the Tribunal and submits that by the first order Tribunal ordered publication of notification as against the petitioners and in the second order Tribunal noticed that notifications were published in the daily Janakantha and the daily Sangram, but nowhere in both the orders th9fe was any sentence as to whether the Tribunal was satisfied that the petitioners were absconding so as to commence trial against them in absentia. Therefore, Mr Hossain concludes that the entire trial was illegal and so the impugned conviction and sentence passed against the petitioners must be held illegal and without jurisdiction. In support of his submission Mr Hossain cites an unreported decision of a Division Bench dated 7-7-97 passed-in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5274 of 1996 (Belayet Howlader vs State). 

 6. Certified copy of the charge-sheet is annexure 'B' to the Rule application. In the charge sheet it was said that the petitioners and three other accused were absconding since the date of occurrence and other two accused were forwarded to the court. It is obviously after looking into the charge sheet Tribunal ordered vide No. 2 dated 25-7-93 publication of notification in two Bengali news- papers directing the accused including the petitioners to appear before the Tribunal within seven days from the date of publication of the notification. Thereafter in the order No.8 dated 7-8-93 learned Tribunal Judge noted that the copies of the newspapers, Daily Janakantha and Daily Sangram, where the said notifications were published, were received in the case record. 

 8. Satisfaction is the mental act and after being satisfied what is done is the result of that mental act. When learned Tribunal Judge ordered publication of the notification in the daily newspapers as prescribed in section 11 of the Anti- Terrorism Act it indicated that the learned Tribunal Judge was mentally satisfied that the accused persons had become absconders. The word satisfaction need not be written before passing order under sub-section (1) of section 11 of the Anti- Terrorism Act for publication of the notification in the daily newspapers. The submission of Mr Hossain is too technical and the absence of the word 'satisfaction' in the order cannot prevent us from looking into the background as can be gathered from the case record leading to the publication of notification. The fact that notification was ordered to be published in the daily newspapers and it was so published cannot be overlooked simply because the learned Tribunal Judge did not state that he obviously accepted the statement in the charge sheet that the accused persons including the petitioners were absconding since the date of occurrence and they could not be arrested and produced before the trial Court by the police. One consequence of the rule of literal construction is that wide word should be given wide construction. 

 9. Unreported decision of a Division Bench cited by Mr Hossain is not applicable in this case. Notification in that case was published in a daily newspaper named 'Dainik Thikana' published from the district of Faridpur whereas the expression mentioned in' section 11 of the Anti-Terrorism Act should mean two national daily newspapers and in that context noticing that the notification was published in a daily newspaper which was 'District based daily newspaper' the Division Bench set aside the conviction and ordered retrial of the case. But in the instant case we find that the notification was published in the two national daily newspapers and, as such, there was no illegality in trying the petitioners' in absentia. We find no substance in this Rule.
